scenarios.title: The Kicker They Drafted
scenarios.text: The club drafts a kicker in the middle rounds. He's watching your every kick from the sideline, taking notes, and he's very polite about it.

choices.label: Give him a show
choices.result: Every practice, a quiet show: long, clean and calm. He takes a lot of notes, and so, you notice, do the coaches.

choices.label: Teach him
choices.result: Your routine, your wind charts, your nerves: you teach him all of it. The room notices, and so does {coach}.

choices.label: Ask {coach} the plan
choices.result: The plan, asked plainly in the hallway. {coach}'s answer is honest: you're the kicker, and he's the future. Both things are true.

scenarios.title: Hurt at Thirty
scenarios.text: An injury in your thirties, a groin strain on a routine kick, and the recovery takes longer than it used to. The trainers keep saying 'at your age', gently.

choices.label: Follow the plan exactly
choices.result: The plan, exactly, for six weeks. It takes longer than it would have at twenty-five, and you come back whole.

choices.label: Push to come back
choices.result: Back two weeks early, and sore. You kick carefully for a month, and the trainers watch every rep like hawks.

choices.label: Take extra time
choices.result: Extra time, on purpose. You come back fresh and a little behind, and your body thanks you for it all season.

choices.label: Use what you learned
choices.result: What you learned last time comes straight back: the order of the exercises, the warning signs, the patience. You're back on schedule and smarter.
choices.lock_text: having been through a hard recovery before

scenarios.title: The New Club at Thirty
scenarios.text: A new club, and the young players already know your name.

choices.label: Earn it anyway
choices.result: You earn it anyway, one practice at a time.

choices.label: Take them to lunch
choices.result: You take the young specialists to lunch the first week.

choices.label: Focus on the job
choices.result: You focus on the job. The rest follows.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Patch
scenarios.text: You wear the captain's patch for the first time, sewn on by the equipment manager that morning. The whole team is watching to see what a kicker does with it.

choices.label: Speak before the first game
choices.result: A speech before the first game, short and true. Your voice shakes on the second sentence, and they listen anyway, all of them.

choices.label: Thank the room
choices.result: Thanks, to every person who voted, one by one. It takes all week and it means more to them than any speech.

choices.label: Lead by example
choices.result: First on the field and last off it, every single day. You never mention the patch once, and nobody needs you to.

scenarios.title: The Holder Retires
scenarios.text: Your longtime holder retires, and the new one is half your age, a backup quarterback with soft hands and no idea how much this matters to you.

choices.label: Build trust fast
choices.result: Every spare minute, spent with the new holder: lunches, film, a hundred extra holds a day. By October the trust is there.

choices.label: Rep it out
choices.result: Holds, hundreds of them, after every practice for a month. Your leg is heavy, and the timing is perfect by the opener.

choices.label: Teach the details
choices.result: The details that took you years to learn, taught in an afternoon: the laces, the lean, the count. The new holder writes them on a wristband.

scenarios.title: The Rookie's Holdout
scenarios.text: A rookie holds out of camp over his contract, and the veterans want you to talk to him. He's twenty-two, he's scared, and his agent is very loud.

choices.label: Talk to him about the long game
choices.result: A long phone call about the long game: careers, reputations, what a room remembers. He signs a week later and thanks you.

choices.label: Stay out of his business
choices.result: His money, his business, you decide. You stay out of it, and the veterans are a little disappointed in their captain.

choices.label: Talk to his family
choices.result: His parents, worried, call you after a mutual friend gives them your number. You talk them through it, and they talk to him.

scenarios.title: The Charity Foundation Gala
scenarios.text: Your foundation holds its first gala. There are round tables, donors in suits, and a ballroom that costs more than you like to think about.

choices.label: Give the speech
choices.result: You give the speech, nervous and honest. It raises more than you hoped, and a donor finds you afterward to double their check.

choices.label: Bring the kids it helps
choices.result: You bring the kids the foundation helps and seat them at the front table. Nobody in the room forgets them, which was the point.

choices.label: Keep it small
choices.result: Small and personal: fewer tables, better food, one true story from the stage. It raises less money, and it feels completely like yours.

choices.label: Tell the story of why
choices.result: Why you started it, all of it, told to a silent ballroom. The donations double that night, and you have to sit down afterward.

scenarios.title: Kindergarten Morning
scenarios.text: Your youngest's first day of kindergarten is a practice day.

choices.label: Ask to come in late
choices.result: You ask {coach} for an hour. You're there for the wave.

choices.label: Do drop-off and run
choices.result: You do drop-off and make it to the meeting with a minute to spare.

choices.label: Go to practice
choices.result: You go to practice and hear about it at dinner.

scenarios.title: The Kid's Team
scenarios.text: Your kid's youth team needs a coach, and everyone looks at you.

choices.label: Coach the team
choices.result: You coach the team. It's the most stressful thing you do all year.

choices.label: Be an assistant
choices.result: You help as an assistant.

choices.label: Cheer from the stands
choices.result: You cheer from the stands.

scenarios.title: The Anniversary Trip
scenarios.text: You and {love_interest} plan a trip for your anniversary, and the club schedules a minicamp.

choices.label: Ask to miss a day
choices.result: You ask to miss a day. The club agrees, grudgingly.

choices.label: Move the trip
choices.result: You move the trip by a week.

choices.label: Go to minicamp
choices.result: You go to minicamp and promise next year.

scenarios.title: The Marriage Counselor
scenarios.text: You and {love_interest} decide to see a counselor, before anything's wrong. It was their idea, and you agreed faster than you expected.

choices.label: Commit to it
choices.result: You commit to it, every other Tuesday, even in season. It's the best thing you do for the marriage, and you say so out loud.

choices.label: Go every other week
choices.result: You go every other week when the schedule allows. It helps, and you learn how differently you two remember the same arguments.

choices.label: Try it once
choices.result: You go to one session to see what it's like. It's harder than practice, and you leave unsure whether you'll go back.

scenarios.title: The Old College Friend's Wedding
scenarios.text: A college friend's wedding brings back the whole old crowd: the dorm, the band you all had, the professor everybody was afraid of. Even {best_friend} is there.

choices.label: Catch up until the lights come on
choices.result: Every old friend, caught up with, until the lights come on. {best_friend} and you close down the dance floor, badly.

choices.label: The ceremony and one dance
choices.result: The ceremony, one dance, and home before eleven. It's lovely, and you're asleep before the band plays the old song.

choices.label: Give an unplanned toast
choices.result: An unplanned toast, when the groom asks, about the night the whole dorm got snowed in. The whole room roars with laughter.

scenarios.title: The Old College Rival Retires
scenarios.text: A kicker you've competed with since college retires, in a short statement on a quiet Tuesday. You've measured yourself against him, quietly, for fifteen long years.

choices.label: Call him
choices.result: A phone call, that night. You talk for an hour about every game you shared, and he admits he always watched your kicks too.

choices.label: Say something public and kind
choices.result: Something kind, said on the record, about his long career. He thanks you the next day by text, and the league notices too.

choices.label: Sit with the news
choices.result: The news, sitting with you for a while. It's closer than it used to be, and you go for a long walk.
